source_name: ÚPSVaR – hromadné prepúšťanie (mass-layoff notification regime)
why_relevant: Employers with 20+ staff must notify the labour office at least one month before mass layoffs. For Bratislava/Košice processor and shared-service hubs, this regime is the statutory early-warning channel for hub downsizing — ahead of any corporate press release.

source_name: Profesia.sk – company job-listing pages (payments employers)
why_relevant: Dominant SK job board. Per-company vacancy pages for Global Payments Europe s.r.o., Global Payments s.r.o. organizačná zložka, Trust Pay a.s. etc. give near-real-time hiring volume and role mix — the cleanest proxy for hub expansion, new function build-outs and quiet freezes.

source_name: Služby zamestnanosti – štátny portál pracovných ponúk (ÚPSVaR job portal)
why_relevant: State vacancy portal; employers report openings to the labour office, so it offers a non-commercial, licence-friendly hiring signal for SK payments employers alongside Profesia.

source_name: Nexi Central Europe (ex SIA Central Europe) – corporate site
why_relevant: Bratislava-headquartered (Röntgenova 1, Petržalka) processor with 250-499 staff, renamed from SIA Central Europe in March 2023. Its own company-data and news pages are the primary channel for management and org announcements at one of the largest payments employers in SK.

source_name: Nexi Slovakia – LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: LinkedIn is where SK payments country managers and hub leads announce appointments before any press release; the company page also exposes headcount trend and open roles.

source_name: Euronet Worldwide – global careers & locations pages
why_relevant: Euronet runs large Slovak operations (Euronet Services Slovakia, ATM/EFT and epay). Its global careers and locations pages are the employer-side channel for Bratislava hub role volume and site presence; the SK site euronet.sk/kontakt.html carries local addresses.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf – Slovakia openings page
why_relevant: DIEBOLD NIXDORF s.r.o. (Mokráň záhon 4, Bratislava; 250-499 staff) is a major ATM-vendor employer in SK. The country openings page tracks service-organisation build-up or contraction directly.

source_name: Global Payments Slovensko – corporate site and contacts
why_relevant: Global Payments operates in SK via Global Payments s.r.o., organizačná zložka (Vajnorská 100/B, Bratislava) plus Global Payments Europe s.r.o. hiring into Bratislava. Local site/contacts pages reveal entity structure and branch-level presence changes.

source_name: Worldline Slovensko – local site (about / contact)
why_relevant: Worldline's Slovak-language country pages document its SK merchant-acquiring/terminal presence and any change in the local operating entity or support footprint; also platobnyterminal.sk.worldline.com as a separate SK-facing property.

source_name: Mastercard Workday careers (CZ/SK roles, Prague-based CEE cluster)
why_relevant: Scheme roles covering Slovakia are typically posted under a Prague/CEE cluster. Postings such as 'Manager, Specialist Sales, Czech Republic & Slovakia' reveal how the scheme structures SK coverage and when a country-facing seat opens — a reliable precursor to a country-manager appointment.

source_name: Finsider.sk – SK banking & payments trade news
why_relevant: Specialist SK finance outlet that covers scheme/issuer switches (e.g. Slovenská sporiteľňa moving from Mastercard to Visa) and payments-company news; such commercial shifts frequently accompany local org and account-team changes.

source_name: TASR OTS – Originálna textová služba (verbatim corporate press releases)
why_relevant: OTS carries companies' own unedited SK press releases, the standard channel through which foreign payments firms announce a Slovak country manager or a Bratislava site decision to the local market.

source_name: tlacove.spravy.info – SK press-release aggregator (fintech tag)
why_relevant: Free aggregator of SK press releases with a fintech tag; useful low-cost complement to paid wires for catching smaller acquirers'/ISOs' leadership and expansion announcements.

source_name: SITA.sk – SK news agency business wire
why_relevant: Second SK news agency; its business section covers company appointments and site decisions, giving redundancy against TASR paywalling.

source_name: FinReg.sk – SK financial-entity register aggregator
why_relevant: Aggregates regulatory and register data for SK financial-sector entities (e.g. Nexi Central Europe by DIČ), providing a convenient cross-index between NBS registrations, IČO/DIČ and corporate identity for the payments population.

source_name: 8h.sk – SK job aggregator (cross-portal vacancy index)
why_relevant: Aggregates vacancies across SK portals by employer name (e.g. Global Payments Europe s.r.o.), giving broader hiring coverage than any single board and a fallback when Profesia rate-limits.

source_name: ifirmy.sk / azet.sk firemné registre – SK business directories
why_relevant: Directory listings hold historical addresses and contact details for payments entities (e.g. Euronet Services Slovakia at Prievozská 4 vs Karadžičova 8), which helps detect office relocations and site changes that no press release announces.

source_name: NBS – Payment institutions and AISP / authorisation requirements section
why_relevant: Sets out what NBS demands of licence applicants, including fit-and-proper and responsible-persons requirements. This is the causal mechanism behind the cell's core hypothesis: a licence application forces named compliance/AML/MLRO and management appointments. Understanding the requirement set lets the collector time hiring expectations off a licence event.

source_name: NBS – Dohľad kryptoaktív (MiCA / CASP supervision and licence decisions)
why_relevant: MiCA has consolidated the Slovak crypto sector hard — NBS states only six licensed CASPs operate in SK against ~700 previously registered actors. Each surviving/incoming licensee must staff named compliance and risk roles, and the losers shed teams; both are hiring/org-change signals for Fumbi-class actors in this cell.

source_name: NBS Fintech / Innovation Hub & FinTech Hub Slovakia section
why_relevant: The regulator's fintech-facing channel; the associated FinTech Hub Slovakia programme publishes cohorts of participating start-ups/scale-ups. Cohort lists are an actor-discovery pointer for exactly the small end this cell covers, and hub participation frequently precedes licence applications and senior hires.

source_name: Obchodný vestník (Commercial Bulletin) – SR
why_relevant: Statutory gazette carrying company notices, capital changes, mergers, liquidations and convocations for SK entities. Complements ORSR by dating corporate restructurings that drive org build-out or team shedding at small payment/crypto firms.

source_name: Praca.sme.sk – job listings (compliance / AML)
why_relevant: Second SK job aggregator with partly non-overlapping inventory; provides redundancy for the hiring signal and catches postings that never reach Profesia. Observed to carry AML/compliance roles from financial employers.

source_name: Finby (formerly TrustPay) – corporate press-release page
why_relevant: Named cell actor. TrustPay — the largest SK-origin payments scale-up — rebranded to finby and, per the sources found, obtained a Malta licence for EU expansion. A rebrand plus a second-jurisdiction licence reliably produces a wave of exec appointments and a new local compliance org; the company's own newsroom is the primary announcement channel. A separate finby.cz 'O společnosti' page exists for the CZ entity.

source_name: Finax – 'Our team' / o nás page
why_relevant: Named cell actor (SK robo-advisor scaling across CEE). Company team pages are the cheapest reliable org-chart diff: adding or removing a named executive is directly observable without any press release. Finax publishes a structured team page in both sk and en.

source_name: Fontech / Startitup.sk – Slovak startup & tech business coverage
why_relevant: High-volume SK startup outlet (with a fintech-leaning Fontech vertical) that reports seed and Series A rounds, state-fund investments and founder stories. Funding announcements here are the trigger event the cell's thesis hangs on — a round covered by Startitup is typically followed by senior hires within weeks.

source_name: Forbes.sk – business and fintech coverage
why_relevant: Higher-credibility SK business outlet that runs named interviews with fintech and neobank CEOs (e.g. the 365.bank CEO on branch strategy) and covers market entries such as Revolut. Interviews are a rich source of forward-looking org and headcount statements.

source_name: TOUCHIT.sk – Slovak tech/fintech product and company coverage
why_relevant: SK tech outlet that covers digital-banking product launches and company milestones (e.g. a 365.bank anniversary retrospective). Product launches are a proxy for engineering-team build-out and often name the responsible executives.

source_name: Kryptomagazín.sk – Slovak crypto trade media
why_relevant: Covers the SK crypto/MiCA licensing shakeout in local language, including which firms survived licensing. For the crypto-and-payments half of this cell (Fumbi and peers), it names actors and licence outcomes that the mainstream business press skips.
